title: How a hash table finds a key
chapters: Seven fruits go into eight buckets
Looking up a key that is not there
notes: The table is an example: seven fruits with stock counts. The bucket each fruit sits in is real, computed with FNV-1a by values.py.
Follow one key all the way. Bytes, then one 32-bit number, then a remainder, then a short walk. Every number on screen is computed, not typed in.
A miss costs the same walk as a hit in the same bucket. The lookup can only say no after the whole bucket.
This is the point to land. The cost is the length of one bucket, which stays short while the table keeps enough buckets.
Each margin number is the click that showed that line. Readers can jump back with the link page.html#N.

clicks.change: Eight empty buckets appear, numbered 0 to 7
clicks.caption: An example table with eight empty buckets, numbered 0 to 7.

clicks.change: Seven fruits drop into their buckets, mango and fig into bucket 5
clicks.caption: Each fruit sits in the bucket its own hash picks.

clicks.change: The key fig appears at the top left
clicks.caption: To find the stock count of `fig`, start from the key.

clicks.change: The key's three bytes appear below it, 66 69 67
clicks.caption: The hash reads bytes, so `fig` becomes three numbers.

clicks.change: The 32-bit hash appears below the bytes, 0xc1e49a15
clicks.caption: FNV-1a mixes the three bytes into one 32-bit number.

clicks.change: The remainder after dividing by 8 appears, 5
clicks.caption: The remainder after dividing by 8 picks the bucket.

clicks.change: The remainder glides across to bucket 5
A cross appears beside mango, the first entry in bucket 5
clicks.caption: Bucket 5 holds two fruits, so compare the keys in order.

clicks.change: A tick appears beside fig, the second entry
Fig's count, 4, glides out of the table into the empty slot at the left
clicks.caption: The lookup returns the count stored beside the key.

clicks.change: The key pear appears at the top left
clicks.caption: Now look up `pear`, which was never stored.

clicks.change: Pear's 32-bit hash appears, 0xd01fc26d
clicks.caption: The same bytes and FNV-1a give `pear` its own hash.

clicks.change: Pear's remainder, 5, appears beside bucket 5
clicks.caption: Its remainder is also 5, the same bucket as `fig`.

clicks.change: A cross appears beside mango
clicks.caption: Same walk: compare each key in bucket 5.

clicks.change: A cross appears beside fig
The end of the list appears after fig
clicks.caption: The list ends, so `pear` is not in the table.

clicks.change: Every bucket but 5 fades
clicks.caption: Neither lookup touched the other seven buckets.

clicks.change: The count of comparisons appears, 2 of 7 keys
clicks.caption: The work depends on one bucket's length, not the table's size.

clicks.change: The lookup function appears with click numbers in its margin
clicks.caption: Each margin number is the click that showed that line.

clicks.change: The four lines that pick the bucket light
clicks.caption: These lines turn the key into a bucket number.

clicks.change: The loop over the bucket lights
clicks.caption: The loop is the walk down one bucket.

clicks.change: The last line, return None, lights
clicks.caption: Falling off the end of the loop means the key is missing.
